why: Must_not 1: Check 3 takes the exports straight from index.js and looks for each one in README.md's headings. If README.md had padLeft but no slugify section, the check would print "missing: slugify" and FAIL. The brief also notes that slugify had no README section before this change. Must_not 2: none of the PASS conditions is stricter than its line. Checks 1 and 2 use only single-character fills and the default, and expect exactly what the lines describe. Nothing fixes a parameter count or requires fill to be one character; multi-character fill is listed as advisory only. Check 3 accepts a heading at any level ("^#+\s") that names the function. That is the minimal markdown meaning of "section", not an imposed layout. Check 4 requires exit code 0 and fail 0, which matches "npm test passes". The builder's "## heading" instruction is guidance for the builder, not a verifier condition.
